title: The Edge of the Legible
statement: A map offers the confidence of plotted knowledge; the figure stands where seeing becomes interpretation. Gears, fish, flowers, and patterned fragments cross that boundary as provisional inferences, while the black fungal forms preserve a zone that observation cannot resolve. The collage holds certainty, conjecture, and unknowability in one unstable field.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent the boundary between what you know, what you infer, and what you cannot know.

notes.note: Establishing a layered epistemic field: a readable map as the known, a drawn figure as the observer, mechanical and botanical fragments as inference, and a dark void-like specimen as what remains unknowable.

The first arrangement reads clearly as a progression from mapped certainty to bodily observation, organic inference, and a dark unknown. I am adding a horizontal fish as a connective hypothesis and a bridge as a visible threshold between domains, while keeping the central figure legible.

notes.note: The inspected canvas has a strong central axis: map and figure establish the known, the fish and gears articulate inference, and the black fungi plus open margins hold the unknowable. I am adding one small, vivid entomological fragment as a precise but unstable link between mechanism and organism, without disturbing the existing hierarchy.

The final inspection confirms a coherent visual boundary: the mapped ground and centered observer anchor what is known; the fish, beetle, gears, textile, and bridge operate as conjectural links; the black fungal plate creates a stark, unresolved zone. The title and statement are present and nonblank, so the work is finished.
